assessment.nobel_worthiness: A discernible change in medicine: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, the active truncated peptide) was converted into long-acting agonists that now treat type 2 diabetes and obesity with cardiovascular and renal benefits. Discovery, mechanism and therapy are all clear and the impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor actions) are decisive on the mechanism; Knudsen led the pharmacological engineering of liraglutide and semaglutide. Mojsov's early identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is an important claim that conflicts with a three-person limit, and Habener is not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent replication and large randomized outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably pressing given the clinical scale.
uncertainties: How to weigh Mojsov's contribution against the three-person limit is unresolved.
Mixed basic and translational credit; I rely on my own recollection of the history rather than verified sources.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality; originality and clinical consequence are high.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and design principles) are the clearest pair. Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials are important but arguably a distinct lineage; Eshhar is not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up; maturity is good, though solid-tumor benefit and toxicity remain open.
uncertainties: Credit for the original CAR concept is missing from the supplied names.
Whether Rosenberg belongs in the same prize is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new organelle-to-nucleus signaling pathway, with the Ire1/Hac1 mechanism defined with clarity; it opened the field of proteostasis and links to diabetes, cancer and neurodegeneration.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and complementarily defined the pathway; a two-person prize is clean and well supported.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed repeatedly over three decades; recognition is mature and not premature. Direct clinical translation is still developing.
uncertainties: The relative weight of the clinical impact is modest compared with therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense correction of SMN2 led to nusinersen, the first disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy and a proof of principle for RNA-targeted drugs in the nervous system.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 target; Bennett led the antisense oligonucleotide chemistry and development. Others (for example Singh, Hua, Adrian Krainer's collaborators) may deserve mention, but the supplied pair is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong randomized trial data; likely timely, though only a decade of follow-up.
uncertainties: Contributions of additional scientists outside the supplied names are not assessable.
Industry-academia credit is partly a corporate matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of Wnt (Int-1) and the pathway it defines is foundational for development, stem cells and cancer; it is broad, original and has lasting impact across fields.
assessment.attribution: Nusse and Varmus identified Int-1 as an MMTV-activated proto-oncogene, and Nusse developed the later Wnt biology. Varmus has already received a prize for a related oncogene discovery, which may weigh against. Wieschaus and Nusslein-Volhard's Wingless genetics were previously recognized, so the allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed, with decades of follow-up. Clinical translation of Wnt modulators remains limited.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for Drosophila patterning and oncogenes complicates the case.
Roles of other Wnt pioneers (for example Moon, McMahon, Brown) are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and successors turned CML from fatal into a chronic condition and established targeted kinase inhibition as a paradigm; the impact is exceptional and the logic is clear.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound program), Druker (clinical proof and trial leadership) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent three-person set. Earlier recognition of the BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Gray, Baltimore) is separate and not included.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with long-term survival data. Possible concern that the prize area has already been touched via oncogene awards and that this is largely translational.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to recognize BCR-ABL cytogenetics first is unclear.
Corporate versus academic credit for the compound is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lgr5 stem-cell biology and the culture of self-organizing intestinal organoids gave a general platform for modelling tissue biology, disease and drug testing.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is clearly the leader; Sato was the first author who established the long-term culture. Two names capture the main contribution; contributions from others (for example Eiraku, Lancaster) are in separate organoid lineages.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and independently reproduced, but translational impact and standardization are still developing, so timing may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical consequence is not yet fully demonstrated.
Whether the organoid concept should be bundled with other stem-cell derived 3D systems is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics changed experimental neuroscience by enabling cell-type-specific, millisecond control of activity with microbial opsins; it is transformative as a method with wide use in physiology.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and neuronal deployment (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetic approach) are all decisive. Six credited names cannot fit within three, so any selection is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Widely validated and mature as a tool; therapeutic translation is early, and the discovery is a method rather than a disease mechanism.
uncertainties: The three-person limit forces exclusion of Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck, which makes attribution highly uncertain.
Method rather than disease-focused discovery may be judged differently by members.
